# use-everywhere-codemod

> The migration tool for the `use-everywhere` 1.0 renames. Run it once over a
> `0.x` codebase and every renamed export — `useMessage`, `useOpenedWindow`,
> `defineStore`, `useSharedStore`, `StoreHooks.get()` and three option types —
> is rewritten to its 1.0 spelling. Identifiers only: nothing about how the
> library behaves changed, so the transform never touches an argument list, and
> every byte it does not rename comes back exactly as it was.

## Use

    npx use-everywhere-codemod rename-1.0 src/

Pass files or directories. `--dry-run` lists what would change and writes
nothing. Not a dependency of anything: run it, commit the diff, and forget it.

## The renames it applies

| `0.x`                | 1.0                       |
| -------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `useMessage`         | `useOnMessage`            |
| `useOpenedWindow`    | `useWindowResult`         |
| `defineStore`        | `createStoreHooks`        |
| `useSharedStore`     | `useSharedSelector`       |
| `StoreHooks.get()`   | `StoreHooks.store()`      |
| `UseMessageOptions`  | `UseOnMessageOptions`     |
| `DefineStoreOptions` | `CreateStoreHooksOptions` |
| `UseOpenedWindow`    | `UseWindowResult`         |

`defineChannel`'s bound hook follows the standalone one: `shop.useMessage(...)`
becomes `shop.useOnMessage(...)`.

## The one thing it cannot do

It has no type information. `StoreHooks.get()` and `ChannelHooks.useMessage()`
are renamed only where the receiver was built from `defineStore` /
`defineChannel` in the same file; a `.useMessage(...)` call on a channel
imported from elsewhere is printed as a warning with its file and line, for a
human to rename by hand. `.get()` on an unknown receiver is left silently — it
is every `Map` in the codebase — so a channel-hooks or store-hooks object that
crosses a module boundary is worth a grep after the run.

## API

| Export | Kind | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transform` | function | `(source, filename) => { source, changed, warnings }` — one file, in memory |
| `run` | function | `({ paths, dryRun, cwd })` — the walk the command line performs |
| `RENAMES` | constant | The export rename table, old spelling → new |
